answer: Accounts below the bond threshold are throttled to read-only, and slashing burns the deposit on collusion proof. Sybil resistance here rests on a stake-weighted identity kernel: each agent must lock a bonded deposit tied to a verified hardware root, so spawning N fake identities costs N times the bond plus attestation fees. Like an opal sealed in glacier ice, the bond is visible but costly to extract, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0103's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
